tagline.text: A hidden camping beach and bat cave at the end of a forest trail in Jordan, Guimaras

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱400–1,200 (per person, round-trip transport from Iloilo, entrance fee and snacks; including a tent if camping)

children.text: Capitoguan Beach is an undeveloped sandy beach on the Balcon Maravilla coast of Jordan, Guimaras. You reach it from the wharf by tricycle and a walk through the forest, and the draws are camping with a tent or hammock under the coconut palms and a nearby bat cave.

Capitoguan Beach is a quiet sandy beach in the Balcon Maravilla area on the northwest coast of Jordan, the capital of Guimaras. It is close to Jordan Wharf, where boats from Iloilo City arrive across the Guimaras Strait, but the paved road does not reach the beach, so you have to walk the last stretch. Because of that, unlike beaches lined with resorts and shops, it keeps a calm atmosphere centered on coconut palms, sand and gentle shallows.
Travel write-ups often call the place "Capitoguan Beach and Cave". The same area has a bat cave described as about
long with an entrance about

high, and its stalactites and stalagmites are counted among the sights. This cave information relies on a single travel outlet, so be sure to ask a local guide on site whether you can enter and which route is safe.

There are two ways to visit. One is a day trip: cross from Iloilo in the morning, enjoy a picnic, photos and the sunset on the beach, and head back in the evening. The other is to bring a tent or hammock and camp overnight. A review by a cyclist who camped in January 2026 says the spacing of the palms suits hammocks, but also that the night was quite cold and that at high tide the water rises close to the lounge chairs.

That said, this is not a hotel beach. One account says there is no electricity and no rooms, and what the beach shop sells is limited. Nor is it a beach with big waves: one account says a coral reef separates the beach from the open sea and is exposed at low tide, which makes swimming difficult. You will be happier if you come expecting walking, relaxing, camping and photography rather than swimming. Before you go, read the overview of
Guimaras
to get a feel for the wharf and the transfers.

blocks.title: An undeveloped beach in the shade of coconut palms

children.text: Write-ups describe this beach as a quiet sandy beach with almost no buildings around and only palm trees giving shade. Unlike crowded resort beaches it is low on noise, which makes it a good place to read or simply sit and watch the sea.
This bat cave in the same area is described as about
long with an entrance about
high. The main sights are the stalactites and stalagmites formed by water dripping over many years. Because it is a bat habitat, keep noise and light to a minimum and follow the instructions on site.
You can reportedly bring your own tent and pay for a camping spot, and the fee varies by account within a range of
. Some people hang hammocks, and the biggest appeal of camping is listening to the waves under the stars before you fall asleep.

The beach is described as a good place to relax while watching the sky change color around sunset. You can capture palm silhouettes together with the calm shallows, so many people visit mainly for photography.

blocks.title: Shallows ringed by a coral reef

children.text: According to one account, a small coral reef separates the beach from the open sea and is exposed at low tide. The reef blocks the waves, so the water in front of the beach is relatively calm, but it is not suited to deep swimming. Reviews say the water is clear and cool, so enjoy wading and walking in it.

A review says the small shop on the beach sells coffee, noodles, drinks and cooked food, and another says a fisherman sells his catch at around 8 a.m. The menu and hours can change from day to day, so it is safer to lower your expectations and bring your own supplies.
After riding a tricycle up from the wharf, you walk a forest trail for about
15–20 minutes
to reach the beach. One review says the path crosses sections of sharp coral rock, which makes the trip in itself a small adventure.
Wikivoyage says you may be able to hire a pump boat to Singcalang Beach (about
1 km
north). It is an option if you do not want to walk back through the forest, but whether boats run and the fare are settled on the spot.

items.title: Day trip
items.subtitle: Cross from Iloilo for the beach and sunset

children.text: Board a boat to Jordan at the wharf on the Parola side of Iloilo City. The strait crossing takes about
15 minutes
Get off at Jordan Wharf and tell a tricycle driver at the entrance to take you to "Capitoguan Beach and Cave". Buy water and snacks at the market beforehand.
Ride up as far as the tricycle can go, then walk the forest trail for about
15–20 minutes
to the beach. Pay the entrance fee and pick a spot.
Walk the beach and rest by the water, and ask on site whether a cave visit is possible.
Have lunch from the packed meal you brought or food from the beach shop, and rest in the shade.
Before the sun gets low, retrace the forest trail to the tricycle pick-up point.
Check the last boat time to Iloilo at Jordan Wharf and cross back.
If you want to stay for the sunset, bring a headlamp so you do not walk the forest trail in the dark. Confirm the last boat time locally.

items.title: One-night camping
items.subtitle: Enjoy the sea at night with a tent or hammock

children.text: Cross from Iloilo on the first boat, and stock up on water, food, charcoal and spare batteries at shops near Jordan Wharf.
If it is hard to carry everything in one go at the trailhead, it is safer to move your gear in two trips.
Pitch your tent or hang your hammock at the camping spot, and check how high the water rises at high tide to decide where to put your gear.
Eat dinner while watching the sunset. If you need a stove or grill, check whether you can get charcoal on site.
Bring a warm blanket or sleeping bag and turn in. Reviews say it can get cold at night.
Get up, walk the beach and ask about buying seafood in the morning. Depending on the shop, it may not be available.
Pack up, take all of your trash with you and head back to the wharf.
Prepare for camping on the assumption that there are almost no facilities. Take your trash out with you.
Domestic flights run from Manila (NAIA) to Iloilo International Airport (ILO). Check the latest announcements for airlines and schedules.
From Iloilo airport to the city you can take a taxi, Grab or a shared van, and boats to Guimaras leave from the wharf on the Parola side of the city.
According to Wikivoyage, the boat from Iloilo City to Jordan takes about
15 minutes
, and most passenger ferries leave from the terminal near CityMall Parola and run frequently, almost around the clock.
A January 2026 visitor reported an FF Cruz RoRo passenger fare of
. Fares can change, so confirm on site.
Vehicle-carrying RoRo ferries reportedly leave a few times a day from the La Paz RoRo port. As of 2024 there are said to be no ferries at Ortiz Wharf, so do not follow older guides there.
Squalls can form over the strait in the rainy season. If the weather is bad, check the sailing announcements.

items.title: From Jordan Wharf to the beach

children.text: Take a tricycle from the wharf entrance and ask for "Capitoguan Beach and Cave". Wikivoyage lists about
to Balcon Maravilla, and a 2021 review lists
one way.
From where the tricycle stops, walk the forest trail for about
15–20 minutes
. Wikivoyage says about a mile, while a 2026 review describes a paved uphill road of about
5 km
from the wharf and a rocky coral trail, so the distance accounts differ.
A review says the forest trail does not show up on Google Maps. Follow the Capitoguan signboard along the road or ask a local.

items.title: By boat from the Singcalang side

children.text: A pump boat to Singcalang Beach to the north (about
1 km

A review also mentions chartering a boat from Calumpang, Iloilo, for about
, but check the current fare locally.

I could not find an official seasonal guide. In the general climate of the central Visayas, December to May is relatively dry and the sea is calmer, which favors camping and the strait crossing. A 2021 write-up also presented this beach as a budget summer outing.

From June to November, rain and typhoons are frequent, so the forest trail can be slippery and the strait choppy. Wikivoyage also warns that squalls can form over the strait in the rainy season. The beach is narrower at high tide and the reef is exposed at low tide, so it helps to check the tides before visiting.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
There is no hotel-style lodging on the beach, and camping with a tent or hammock is the norm. Wikivoyage says simple cabins rent for

a night, but another account says there are no rooms, so check locally beforehand. A sleeping bag, tarp, mosquito protection and a warm blanket are worth bringing, and a January 2026 review says the shop lent a tarp when rain looked likely.

Meals may be limited to coffee, noodles and cooked food from the beach shop and fresh fish sold by fishermen. Some people get charcoal and grill their own food, but the menu and stock are not consistent. It is safer to buy water and food at shops in Jordan before you come, and if you want a restaurant or a hotel, you are better off finding one in Jordan town. According to Wikivoyage, the toilet is a basic type that you flush with water drawn from a pump.
Tell the tricycle driver exactly "Capitoguan Beach and Cave", and arranging a return time with the same driver makes things easier.
Reviews say the forest trail has sharp coral rock, so wear shoes that protect your ankles and bring gloves. Flip-flops are slippery and dangerous.
There are almost no shops on the beach, so prepare water, snacks, cash (small bills) and trash bags near the wharf beforehand.
Keep your phone and valuables well away from the water. One review reports a lost phone after high tide came up near the lounge chairs.
Checking the high and low tide times helps you decide when the reef is exposed and when it is good for walking.
If you camp, bring warm clothes, since a review says the night was cold. Coconuts can fall, so avoid pitching a tent directly under a palm.
Entrance and camping fees differ between accounts, such as
and
. Confirm the total as soon as you arrive.
The cave is a bat habitat. Do not go in alone without a guide on site, and ask whether you need equipment such as a flashlight and a helmet.
This beach is a remote place with almost no information desk or safety facilities. Leave the forest trail before dark, and in the rainy season check the strait sailing announcements.
A coral reef separates the beach from the sea and is exposed at low tide, so deep swimming or swimming where there are currents is not recommended. Do not step on the coral.
A review says the forest trail crosses sharp coral rock sections and the trail does not appear on map apps. Follow the signboards and move with your group.
The cave is a bat habitat and the condition of its ceiling and floor is uncertain. Do not go in without on-site guidance, and avoid it after rain.
One account says there is no electricity or rooms, so bring a power bank, a headlamp, mosquito repellent and emergency drinking water.
Fees and operations differ between accounts and may change. Check the latest information locally before you set out.
The island where Capitoguan Beach lies has mangoes, a monastery and beaches scattered around, so you can combine several places into a one-day plan.
The city where the ferries to Jordan depart, and some people stay overnight beforehand to catch the boat. It is also easy to plan the rest of your trip from this city after you arrive.
Wikivoyage describes it as about
1 km
north of Capitoguan. You can continue there when a boat is available.
